comments.author: @Fire_Token
comments.text: People like to say that we don't have a clear definition of what AGI really is, but that's not true. Until relatively recently, AI were only trained to perform one specific task. You could have a computer that could beat the world champion at chess, but would have no idea about how to change a tire or debate politics. When the idea for 'general' AI came about, legacy AI systems were rebranded as 'narrow' AI (in order to distinguish it from general AI). Then people started trying to change the definition of AGI and introducing new terms like ASI. However, the term AGI really just means AI that isn't narrow, and can perform well at a general range of tasks. By that definition we've had AGI for several years now. But due to licensing concerns between Microsoft, OpenAI, and Elon Musk... legal shenanigans are being performed with the terminology, as you've covered on this channel already @Wes Roth.
